oneLiner: 每笔交易都同时记“借”与“贷”两方、金额相等——有借必有贷，借贷必相等。
oneLinerEn: Every transaction is posted to both a debit and a credit of equal amount — for every debit there must be an equal credit.
detail: 意大利数学家卢卡·帕乔利 1494 年在《算术、几何、比与比例概要》中系统描述了威尼斯商人的这套记法，被尊为“会计学之父”。其要义是任何一笔经济业务都同时影响至少两个账户，且“借方合计恒等于贷方合计”，于是账簿能靠试算平衡自查是否记错。它把记账从零散的流水变成一套自我约束的符号系统，是财务报表、审计乃至整个现代商业计量的地基；难点在于“借贷”只是“左／右”的记账方向，与“借钱／贷款”的日常含义无关，初学者极易被字面误导。
detailEn: In 1494 the Italian mathematician Luca Pacioli systematised the bookkeeping of Venetian merchants in his Summa and is honoured as the 'father of accounting'. Its core is that every transaction touches at least two accounts and that total debits always equal total credits, so a trial balance can self-check for errors. It turned scattered records into a self-disciplining notation — the ground under financial statements, auditing and modern business measurement. The trap: 'debit' and 'credit' here mean only the left and right sides of a ledger, not borrowing and lending, which misleads beginners.

oneLiner: 资产 = 负债 + 所有者权益——一行同时说清“有什么”和“谁的钱”，是复式记账的骨架。
oneLinerEn: Assets = liabilities + equity — one line says both what you own and who has a claim on it, the spine of double-entry.
detail: 它是复式记账得以自动配平的数学根据：企业拥有的每一项资产，钱要么来自债权人（负债），要么来自股东投入与留存（所有者权益），所以两边天然相等、任何交易都只能在等式内部此消彼长，不会打破平衡。利润会通过留存收益并入权益，把利润表与资产负债表串起来。它看似平庸，却决定了每张凭证如何拆分成借贷分录；理解了资产等于负债加权益，再看资产负债表就不再是死记科目，而是看懂资金来龙去脉的一张因果图。
detailEn: It is the mathematical reason double-entry self-balances: every asset a firm holds was funded either by creditors (liabilities) or by owners' capital and retained earnings (equity), so the two sides are equal by construction and no transaction can break that balance — it only shifts amounts within the equation. Profit flows into equity as retained earnings, linking the income statement to the balance sheet. Plain-looking, it dictates how each entry is split into debit and credit; once 'assets = liabilities + equity' clicks, the balance sheet stops being memorised accounts and becomes a map of where money came from and went.

term: 权责发生制与收付实现制
oneLiner: 收入与费用在“赚到／发生的那一刻”入账，而不是等现金到账才记——这才叫配比。
oneLinerEn: Revenue and expense are booked when earned and incurred, not when cash moves — that matching is the whole point.
detail: 收付实现制只在现金进出时记账，简单、贴近兜里有没有钱，但会把业绩扭曲到收款日：本月卖出的货要等下月回款才算收入。权责发生制则按归属期记录——收入在赚取时确认、费用在为产生该收入而发生时确认，二者配比，于是应收账款、应付账款、预收预付这些科目应运而生，利润更能反映一段经营的真实成绩。代价是它依赖估计与判断（坏账、折旧、收入确认时点），也给提前确认收入、递延费用留下操纵空间。正因如此，读懂一家公司要利润表与现金流量表对照：权责发生制看赚没赚，收付口径看钱到没到。
detailEn: Cash basis records only when money moves — simple and close to whether the pocket has cash, but it warps performance to the settlement date: goods sold this month count as revenue only when paid next month. Accrual basis records by the period to which items belong — revenue when earned, expense when incurred to earn it, matched together — which is why receivables, payables and prepayments exist and why profit better reflects a stretch of real operating effort. The price is reliance on estimates and judgement (bad debts, depreciation, revenue-recognition timing) and the room it leaves to pull revenue forward and defer cost. Hence read a firm by pairing the income statement with the cash-flow statement: accrual shows whether you earned, cash shows whether the money arrived.

oneLiner: 同一笔生意，全世界要按同一套记账语法来做表，数字才可比、可信、能被审计。
oneLinerEn: The same deal must be cast in one grammar of bookkeeping so numbers across firms and borders are comparable, credible and auditable.
detail: 没有统一准则，各公司自选折旧法、收入确认口径，报表就成了可以打扮的化妆术，投资者无从比较。会计准则（美国 GAAP、国际财务报告准则 IFRS）规定交易如何确认、计量、列报与披露，让不同企业、不同年份的数字落在同一把尺子上，是资本市场信任的基础设施。两者路数略有不同：GAAP 更规则导向、条文明细，IFRS 更原则导向、强调实质与职业判断，多年来一直在趋向协调而非完全合并。准则也在相关性与如实反映、可比、可验证、及时之间权衡，并受重要性、一致性等约束；它永远追不上金融创新，所以按准则做表是可信的底线，却不等于生意的真实价值。
detailEn: Without common rules each firm picks its own depreciation and revenue-recognition method, and statements become makeup that can be dressed up — investors cannot compare. Accounting standards (US GAAP, and IFRS) prescribe how transactions are recognised, measured, presented and disclosed, putting numbers from different firms and years on one ruler; they are the trust infrastructure of capital markets. The two differ in temperament — GAAP more rules-based and detailed, IFRS more principles-based, leaning on substance and judgement — long converging rather than fully merging. Standards trade relevance against faithful representation, comparability, verifiability and timeliness, bounded by materiality and consistency; they always lag financial innovation, so 'made to standard' is a floor of credibility, not the same as a business's true worth.

oneLiner: 会计主体、持续经营、会计分期、货币计量四个前提，加上谨慎、配比、实质重于形式等原则。
oneLinerEn: Four premises — entity, going concern, periodicity, monetary measurement — plus prudence, matching and substance over form.
detail: 整套记账建立在四个默认前提上：会计主体（把公司和老板个人分开）、持续经营（假定不会马上清算，才敢按使用年限折旧）、会计分期（人为切成年度季度来考核）、货币计量（只记能用钱衡量的事，人才、口碑进不了表）。在其上运行一组原则：历史成本（按买入价记，客观却可能过时）、配比（费用跟着它带来的收入走）、充分披露（表外附注补足信息）、谨慎稳健（不高估资产与利润、不低估负债）、实质重于形式（按经济实质而非合同外衣入账，防钻空子）、重要性与一致性（小事可从简，口径不能年年乱改）。它们合起来回答数字该信到什么程度，也是审计与管理层博弈的规则场。
detailEn: The whole edifice rests on four default premises: the accounting entity (separate the firm from its owner), going concern (assume no imminent liquidation, so you may depreciate over useful life), periodicity (carve time into years and quarters to measure) and monetary measurement (record only what money can weigh — staff and goodwill stay off the books). On them run a set of principles: historical cost (book at purchase price — objective yet possibly stale), matching (expense follows the revenue it produced), full disclosure (notes fill what the face omits), prudence (do not overstate assets and profit or understate liabilities), substance over form (record by economic reality, not the contract's wrapper, to close loopholes), and materiality and consistency (sweat the small stuff, never reshuffle the basis year to year). Together they answer how far the numbers can be trusted and set the arena where auditors and management play by the same rules.

oneLiner: 一张对外交代（给投资者与税局），一张对内决策（给经理与团队）——同一套账，两种服务对象。
oneLinerEn: One faces outward (investors, tax), one faces inward (managers, teams) — the same books, two audiences.
detail: 财务会计面向企业外部：按准则把已发生的经营固化成三大报表，供投资者、债权人、监管与税务阅读，强调客观、可比、可审计，格式相对固定。管理会计面向企业内部：不受准则约束，为定价、投产、考核与预算服务，看未来、看细分（产品线、部门、客户），手段包括本量利、作业成本、责任中心与预算控制。两者共用同一套原始凭证与账簿，只是一个向后、对外、讲规矩，一个向前、对内、讲有用。财务会计算经营成果长什么样，管理会计问下一步该怎么走；读懂企业既要会看对外报表的诚实，也要会挑对内数据的相关。
detailEn: Financial accounting looks outward: under the standards it fixes what has happened into the three statements for investors, creditors, regulators and tax authorities to read, prized for objectivity, comparability and auditability in a largely set format. Management accounting looks inward: unbound by the standards, it serves pricing, production, appraisal and budgeting, thinking ahead and by segment (product line, department, customer) with tools like cost-volume-profit, activity-based costing, responsibility centres and budget control. Both draw on the same source documents and ledgers — one is backward, outward and rule-bound, the other forward, inward and usefulness-driven. Financial accounting computes what the result looks like; management accounting asks what to do next; reading a firm takes both the honesty of the external report and the relevance of the internal number.

oneLiner: 由独立的第三方替公众验真报表，靠的不是逐笔重算，而是内控、抽样与职业怀疑。
oneLinerEn: An independent third party verifies the statements for the public — not by re-adding every line but through controls, sampling and professional scepticism.
detail: 所有权与经营权分离后，外人凭什么信管理层自报的数字？审计就是补上这道信任缺口：外部审计师以独立身份按准则核查报表是否在所有重大方面公允反映，出具无保留、保留乃至否定或无法表示意见的报告，为资本市场提供可信背书。它不逐笔重算，而是评估并测试内部控制——职责分离、授权审批、实物盘点、对账复核——在薄弱处加大抽样。审计给的是合理保证而非绝对保证，抽样与判断意味着错报可能漏网。另一侧的舞弊三角（压力、机会、自我合理化）提醒：账做得平不等于事干净，制度上要堵住既经手又记账的机会，文化上要松动合理化的土壤。审计与准则相互支撑——准则定义该怎么记，审计核查是否真这么记。
detailEn: Once ownership separates from control, why should outsiders trust the numbers management reports? Auditing closes that trust gap: an external auditor, independent by standing, tests under the standards whether the statements are fairly presented in all material respects and issues an opinion — unqualified, qualified, or adverse and disclaimer — giving capital markets a credible endorsement. It does not re-add every entry but evaluates and tests internal control — segregation of duties, authorisation, physical counts, reconciliations — sampling harder where control is weak. Audit offers reasonable, not absolute, assurance, so sampling and judgement let some misstatements slip. The fraud triangle — pressure, opportunity, rationalisation — is the other warning: books can balance while the business is dirty, so systems must deny the chance to both handle and record an asset, and culture must starve the excuses. Standards and audit lean on each other — standards say how to book it, audit checks whether it was.

oneLiner: 资产负债表拍“快照”、利润表记“一段成绩”、现金流量表看“真金白银的进出”。
oneLinerEn: The balance sheet is a snapshot, the income statement a season's score, the cash-flow statement the actual money in and out.
detail: 三张报表是一家公司的运行说明书，各答不同的问题：资产负债表是某一时点的照片——家底与欠账；利润表与现金流量表是一段时间的电影——前者按权责发生制记账规则算赚了多少，后者只认真金白银的进出。读的关键在勾稽：利润不等于现金——收入一记、应收账款越堆越厚，利润表好看，现金流量表立刻现形；而现金流又分经营、投资、筹资三段：主业在造血还是失血、扩张还是收缩、钱靠借与股还是还回去。“利润是意见，现金是事实”：成熟企业的经营现金流常常远超净利润（折旧从不划出银行账户），成长期企业则常反过来。三表齐好看而经营现金流始终偏薄，就要查它是不是靠筹资流入在妆点——现金流量表是三张里最难造假的一张，可它也真被造过：雷曼在季末把近五百亿美元回购从筹资包装成经营流入，让债消失、钱像主业挣来的。
detailEn: The three statements are one company's operations manual, each answering a different question. The balance sheet is a point-in-time photograph: what the firm owns and what it owes on the reporting date, the difference being what shareholders truly own. The income statement and the cash-flow statement are films over a period — the first counts profit under accrual rules, the second records only money that actually moved. Read them together, because profit is not cash: revenue booked while receivables age looks excellent on the income statement until the cash statement shows the truth. Cash itself comes in three streams — the core business generating or consuming money, investing expanding or shrinking capacity, financing bringing in borrowing and equity, or paying them back. 'Profit is an opinion, cash is a fact': a mature firm's operating cash flow often dwarfs net profit because depreciation never left the bank account, while a growth firm may show the reverse. When all three look beautiful yet operating cash stays thin, check whether financing inflows are dressing it up — the cash statement is the hardest to fake, yet even it has been faked: Lehman Brothers shuffled close to fifty billion dollars of month-end repurchases so that liabilities vanished and cash appeared to have been earned by the business itself.

oneLiner: 资产 = 负债 + 所有者权益——某一时点“有什么”必然等于“谁出的钱”。
oneLinerEn: Assets = liabilities + equity — at a point in time, what you have must equal who funded it.
detail: 资产负债表把资金的去向与来源摊在一张平面上：左边资产按流动性从现金、应收、存货、设备一路排到商誉；右边先排欠人的（短借、长债、应付，按到期日序），余下是股东自己的（股本、留存收益、其他综合收益）。“资产＝负债＋所有者权益”由复式记账的构造保证必平——所以它其实是体检单：看三样，流动资金的净头寸（流动资产够不够抵流动负债）、杠杆的厚度（债是净资产的几倍）、资产的质量（商誉是不是买贵了并购的收据、应收与存货有没有在发霉）。局限也写在“表”字里：早年置办的资产按历史成本挂着，一块地可能记着半世纪前的价；品牌与团队难入账，旗舰门店也许身无分文；租赁在 IFRS 16 之前长期躲在表外，安然更把成堆的债塞进表外实体——照片拍完即塌。所以它回答“还得起吗、还剩多少”，“到底值多少”要靠另外两张表和市场一起作答。
detailEn: A balance sheet lays sources and uses of capital on one plane. Assets, the uses, run left by liquidity — cash, receivables, inventory, plant, then goodwill; the right side shows where the money came from: first what is owed to others (short-term borrowings, bonds, payables, ordered by maturity), beneath that owners' equity — paid-in capital, retained earnings, accumulated other income. 'Assets = liabilities + equity' must hold by construction, which double-entry bookkeeping guarantees. As the firm's health check, read three things: the net position of working capital (current assets against current liabilities), the thickness of leverage (debt as a multiple of net assets), and the quality of the assets (whether goodwill is the receipt for overpaid acquisitions, whether receivables and inventory are ageing). The limits lie in the word 'sheet': old assets sit at historical cost, so land may be booked at prices decades past; brands and teams rarely appear, so a flagship may show scant net assets; leases stayed off-balance before IFRS 16, and Enron hid whole mountains of debt in off-balance-sheet partnerships — the photograph collapsed the moment it was taken. The balance sheet answers 'can it pay, what remains'; whether it is worth anything requires the other two statements, and the market, to say together.

oneLiner: 收入−成本−费用=利润,记录一段时间的经营成绩;但“利润”按权责发生制算,不等于收到现金。
oneLinerEn: Revenue minus cost and expenses equals profit over a period — but accrual 'profit' is not cash collected.
detail: 利润表是一道扣除漏斗：营收减销得毛利，再减营业费用（销管研、折旧摊销）得营业利润，加减非营业项、扣利息与税得净利。每一层都是一个诊断口：毛利率讲产品的竞争力与定价权，营业利润率讲组织的效率，净利率里还掺着财务结构与税负。失真的最大来源是权责发生制的时点裁量——收入何时算挣到、费用何时算发生，都可以商量：提前确认、塞货给渠道（渠道压货）、把费用改资本化、拉长折旧年限、处置收益当经常性利润。安然靠“纸面利润”运转多年，世界通讯把经营性的线路租用费资本化，数十亿美元日常成本从账上消失。所以读它配三问：收入增长是否伴随应收增得更快（销量三倍、应收十倍是经典红灯）、净利是否伴随经营现金流、经常性利润与一次性损益有没有分开。营收是龙骨，毛利是船身，净利是船舱——舱里进水的坏消息，往往在龙骨处就开始渗了。
detailEn: The income statement is a subtraction funnel: revenue minus cost of goods sold gives gross profit, minus operating expenses — selling, administration, research, depreciation — gives operating profit, plus or minus non-operating items, minus interest and tax gives net profit. Every layer is a diagnostic: gross margin speaks of product competitiveness and pricing power, operating margin of organisational efficiency, net margin adds financial structure and tax. The biggest source of distortion is accrual timing — when revenue counts as earned and when costs count as incurred are both negotiable: recognition pulled forward, channel stuffing, expenses capitalised, depreciation lives stretched, one-off gains booked as recurring profit. Enron ran on 'phantom profits' for years; WorldCom capitalised line-lease fees to keep billions of dollars of ordinary operating cost off the books. So read the funnel with three questions: does revenue growth come with receivables growing faster (sales tripling while receivables grow tenfold is a classic red flag), does profit come with operating cash flow, are recurring profits separated from one-off gains. Revenue is the keel, gross profit the hull, net income the cabin — water reaching the cabin usually began seeping at the keel long before.

oneLiner: “现金为王”:利润是观点,现金是事实;经营、投资、筹资三条现金流讲清钱真正怎么转。
oneLinerEn: 'Cash is king': profit is an opinion, cash a fact — operating, investing and financing flows show how money really moves.
detail: 许多倒闭的企业账上有利润，只是先没了现金——亏损是慢性病，断流是急症。现金流量表把真钱分三段：经营（间接法从净利润出发，加回折旧等非现金项、再调营运资金变动，量的是主业造血）、投资（购置或回收产能，扩张还是收缩）、筹资（借款、还债、分红、回购、发股）。三段符号构成健康图谱：经营正、投资负、筹资微负是成熟奶牛；经营正、投资负、筹资正是靠外部输血的扩张；经营与投资俱正、筹资负是在收缩回馈；经营投资俱负、筹资正最危险——借钱撑增长，信贷一紧就知道谁在裸泳。自由现金流（经营现金流减资本开支）才是分红、回购与现金流估值真正的源头。妆点要防：季末突击回款、把应收保理卖出都能人为垫高经营段，雷曼的“回购 105”更把抵押借款记成卖断。所以拿利润与现金流对比：利润是意见，现金是事实；事实好看得反常时，去查上一季度的事实。
detailEn: Many failed firms were profitable on paper; they simply ran out of cash first — losses are a chronic disease, cash is the acute attack. The statement lays real money in three compartments: operating (net profit plus non-cash items like depreciation, adjusted for working-capital swings — the core business's self-funding), investing (buying or selling capacity), financing (borrowing, repaying, dividends, buybacks, issuing shares). The sign pattern is a health chart: positive, negative, slightly negative marks a mature cash cow; positive, negative, positive is expansion on external drips; positive, positive, negative is shrinking and returning money; negative, negative, positive is the danger zone — growth bought with borrowed money, and when credit tightens you see who was swimming naked. Free cash flow, operating cash minus capital expenditure, is what ultimately funds dividends, buybacks and any valuation by discounted cash. Watch the dressing: quarter-end collections and receivable factoring flatter the operating line, and Lehman's 'Repo 105' booked borrowing against collateral as an outright sale. So set profit beside cash: profit is an opinion, cash a fact — and when the fact looks too good, check last quarter's fact.

oneLiner: 固定成本 ÷ 单位边际贡献 = 保本销量;越过它,每一单才开始赚钱。
oneLinerEn: Fixed cost divided by unit contribution gives the break-even volume; past it, each sale starts earning.
detail: 盈亏平衡把成本拆成两堆——房租、设备、人头这类不看产量的固定成本，与材料、包装、佣金这类随件走的变动成本——然后回答最朴素的生意问题：卖多少才不亏。公式只一行：平衡量＝固定成本÷单件贡献边际（单价减单件变动）。设固定成本一年一百万、单价一百、变动六十，贡献四十，就得卖两万五千件；此后每多卖一件，四十元整个落进利润口袋。它的威力在敏感性：降价到九十，贡献只剩三十，同一条平衡线跳到三万三千三百件——价格降一成、平衡负担升三分之一；成本省一元易、价格降十元难，这正是“拼价值不拼价”的算术底子。前提也要说清：相关区间内单价与单件成本线性、产品结构稳定、产等于销不被存货吸收；多产品得按加权贡献算。高固定成本生意（航空、晶圆厂、软件）经营杠杆大——过线利润狂奔、线下亏损雪崩，平衡线就是生死线；增长行业讲“四十法则”，本质是把盈亏平衡思想放大到烧钱与造血的速度配比上。
detailEn: Break-even analysis splits cost two ways — fixed (rent, plant, headcount that ignore output) and variable (materials, packaging, commissions that follow every unit) — then answers the plainest business question: how many units must we sell to lose nothing. One line of formula: break-even volume = fixed cost ÷ unit contribution (price minus unit variable cost). With a million in fixed cost, price one hundred, variable sixty, contribution forty, you must sell twenty-five thousand units — and every unit beyond puts the full forty into profit. Its power is sensitivity: cut price to ninety and contribution falls to thirty, so the same line jumps to thirty-three thousand three hundred — a ten-percent price cut raises the load by a third; saving one yuan on cost is easy, cutting ten on price is ruinous, the arithmetic behind competing on value rather than price. The assumptions deserve equal clarity: within the relevant range, price and unit cost behave linearly, the product mix holds, and production equals sales with no inventory soaking absorption; multiple products require a weighted contribution. High-fixed-cost trades — airlines, fabs, software — carry high operating leverage: above the line profits sprint, below it losses cascade, so the line is a life line; when growth firms talk of the 'rule of forty', they are scaling the same thinking up to the ratio of burning and self-funding.

oneLiner: 流动比率看偿债、负债率看杠杆、周转率看效率、毛利率看定价权。
oneLinerEn: Current ratio for solvency, leverage for debt, turnover for efficiency, margin for pricing power.
detail: 比率把一个数除以另一个数，把绝对值标准化，小企业得以与巨头比、今年得以与去年比。大致五族：偿债（流动、速动比率、利息保障——离违约有多远）、杠杆（负债率、权益倍数——账单到底谁在付）、效率（资产周转、应收与存货天数，再加现金转换周期＝回款天＋存货天－付款天，负值意味着拿供应商的钱做生意）、盈利（毛利、净利、资产回报）、成长（收入与利润的同比）。三重提醒：单个比率无意义，要拿历年、行业、对手三角互证——流动比率二在零售健康、在重工危险；拆开才见驱动，杜邦把净资产收益拆成净利率×周转×杠杆，一眼看出回报挣在谁的手艺上；比率是数字，数字是人做的——季末突击回款、费用资本化、应收出表、长债换短借，都能短期美化它。比率是路灯不是真相：灯照亮该看哪里，灯下有没有宝，要回到报表与生意本身。
detailEn: Ratios divide one number by another to standardise the absolute, letting a small firm compare with a giant and this year compare with last. There are about five families: solvency (current and quick ratios, interest coverage — how far from default), leverage (debt share, equity multiple — who is really paying), efficiency (asset turns, receivable and inventory days, and the cash-conversion cycle = collection days + inventory days − payment days, where a negative means running the business on suppliers' money), profitability (gross, net, return on assets), and growth. Three cautions travel with them. A single ratio means nothing: triangulate against history, industry and peers — a current ratio of two is healthy in retail, dangerous in heavy engineering. The deeper the decomposition the clearer the driver: DuPont splits return on equity into margin × turns × leverage, revealing whose craft the return is earned by. And ratios are numbers made by people: quarter-end collections, capitalising expenses, selling receivables off-balance, swapping long-term debt for short-term all flatter them briefly. Ratios are streetlamps, not truths — they show where to look; whether there is treasure under the light is answered by the statements and the business itself.

oneLiner: 回报率把收益除以投入,让不同规模、不同项目能用同一把尺子比较。
oneLinerEn: Return over input lets projects and firms of different size be measured on one ruler.
detail: 两个比率回答两类问题：ROI 问“这笔投入整体划不划算”，口径宽到万物皆可算；ROE 问“股东的每一块钱每年生多少钱”。它们真正的杀伤力都在口径上：ROI 的分子含不含机会成本、分母算不算已沉没的人与时间、窗口取一年还是三年，每种写法都能把同一个项目算成好看或难看；所以立项评审先对齐定义再看数字。ROE 则被杜邦拆成三乘——净利率乘资产周转率乘权益杠杆——同是 15% 的回报，可能是高端薄利、可能是白菜价靠快转、也可能纯粹是六倍杠杆堆出来的，三种生意的脆弱程度天差地别。账面 ROE 还藏着杠杠：回购与分红把权益分母越做越小，利润率没动、比率自升，航空与快消常年在十几上下并不罕见。所以比较公司前先同口径、同时长、同市场利率环境，再谈高下——比率是提问的好工具，直接当答案就危险了。
detailEn: The two ratios answer different questions: ROI asks whether a given outlay was worth it in the round, elastic enough that almost anything can be scored; ROE asks how much cash each shareholder dollar earns in a year. Their real bite is in the definitions. For ROI, whether the numerator carries opportunity cost, whether the denominator counts sunk people and time, and whether the window is one year or three can each flip the same project between handsome and ugly, which is why a review should settle the definition before reading the number. ROE is best read through the DuPont product — margin times asset turnover times equity leverage — because an identical 15 percent may come from premium margins, from selling cheap and fast, or from pure six-to-one gearing, and those three businesses differ wildly in fragility. Book ROE hides another trick: buybacks and dividends shrink the equity denominator, so the ratio climbs while profitability is unchanged, which is why airlines and consumer staples sit in the teens without scandal. Compare firms only after aligning definition, horizon and the prevailing interest-rate environment; a ratio is an excellent instrument for asking questions and a dangerous one to accept as an answer.

oneLiner: 先算清“服务一个客户赚不赚”:客户终身价值要显著大于获客成本。
oneLinerEn: Before scaling, check one customer pays: lifetime value should clearly exceed the cost to acquire it.
detail: 亏损换增长本身不是罪，罪的是算不清一单到底赚不赚钱。单位经济把生意压缩成两个数：获取成本，即把一位客户带来平均花多少（含补贴、广告与销售人力）；生命周期价值，即这位客户在离前总共贡献多少毛利。常被引用的健康线是价值对成本三倍起——因为毛利还要扣掉管理与研发，一倍回本等于白干；另一半是回本周期，三个月算健康、十八个月则多半是在替未来融资。三个坑都在分母里：生命周期价值靠“留存不变”的假设外推，而留存曲线几乎必弯；获取成本不含品牌与渠道的公共投入，每家都报自家的显得人人健康；规模上来后获客会从便宜的自然流量转向昂贵投放，成本越做越高。所以真正的判据不是比值而是曲线：逐月留存、逐季毛利、分渠道成本分开看——比值只用来向投资人讲一个可以证伪的故事。
detailEn: Growing while losing money is not the sin; the sin is not knowing whether one order makes money. Unit economics compresses a business into two numbers: acquisition cost, what it takes on average to land a customer including subsidies, advertising and sales headcount, and lifetime value, the gross profit that customer contributes before churning. The oft-cited healthy line is three-to-one, because gross profit must still carry overhead and research, so breaking even at one-to-one means working for nothing; the other half is payback period, where three months is healthy and eighteen is usually financing the future out of hope. All three traps sit in the denominator: lifetime value is extrapolated from an assumed flat retention curve when retention almost always bends; acquisition cost excludes shared brand and channel investment, so every cohort looks healthy in isolation; and as scale grows, acquisition shifts from free word of mouth to paid placement, pushing the cost up over time. The real test is therefore curves, not ratios — retention by month, margin by quarter, cost split by channel — while the ratio itself serves mainly to tell investors one claim that can be falsified.

oneLiner: 今天的一块钱比明天的一块钱值钱——折现把不同时点的现金流放到同一天比较。
oneLinerEn: A dollar today beats a dollar tomorrow — discounting brings cash flows at different times onto one date to compare.
detail: 今天的一百块与一年后的一百块不是一回事：钱可投资故有机会成本，物价在上行，未来的兑现又带风险。贴现就是把未来的金额按一个比率折算回今天，比率每高一格，越靠后的现金流被砍得越狠——所以它对长周期项目（基建、研发、气候政策）几乎是生死开关，争论常集中在该用 3% 还是 8%。净现值把项目全部现金流折到今天再减投入，大于零才创造价值；内含报酬率是令其归零的那个贴现率，好读但易误用：非常规现金流可能有多个解，也不能直接拿它比较规模悬殊的项目。两个日常误用值得点名：一是拿名义利率当贴现率却忘扣通胀，把幻觉当收益；二是把“折现”当成对未来不确定性的惩罚——风险应进贴现率或进情景，不该再在现金流上扣一遍。它是估值、资本预算与长期决策的共同地基。
detailEn: A hundred today is not a hundred next year: money can be invested, so it carries an opportunity cost, prices drift upward, and future receipts are uncertain. Discounting converts future amounts back to today at some rate, and every point added to that rate hacks harder at distant cash — which makes the choice almost lethal for long-dated projects (infrastructure, research, climate policy), where arguments live on whether to use three percent or eight. Net present value discounts every cash flow of a project to today and subtracts the outlay; only a positive figure creates value. The internal rate of return is the discount rate that drives it to zero — easy to quote, easy to misuse: unconventional flow patterns admit multiple solutions, and the rate cannot rank projects of very different size. Two everyday errors deserve naming: using a nominal rate while forgetting inflation, which books an illusion as gain, and treating discounting as a punishment for uncertainty — risk belongs in the rate or in the scenarios, not deducted a second time from the cash itself. This is the shared foundation of valuation, capital budgeting and long-horizon choice.

oneLiner: 别只盯财务——从财务、客户、内部流程、学习成长四个视角平衡地度量与驱动战略。
oneLinerEn: Look beyond finance — measure and steer strategy across four views: financial, customer, internal process, learning and growth.
detail: 卡普兰与诺顿 1992 年在《哈佛商业评论》提出，起点是一个旧常识：财务指标是滞后结果，还容易被短期操纵，而真正创造价值的过程发生在报表看不见处。解法是把一张仪表盘扩成四个视角——财务（结果）、客户（如何被价值感知）、内部流程（哪些环节必须做到卓越）、学习与成长（员工能力、信息与系统）——四格不作平均主义并列，而是自下而上串成因果链：员工胜任才有流程称职，流程称职才有客户买单，客户买单才有财务结果，环环都可指认。它顺带纠正一个更普遍的误读：财务是果不是因，把利润目标直接分解到人人头上的利润指标，等于让果实去浇树。领先与滞后指标从此配套——滞后的用来确认战略是否兑现，领先的使用来说明战略是否成立。失败模式同样经典：把它做成又一个考核报表，每格塞十个指标、无人据以行动。计分卡只在战略已清晰到能翻译成目标与量尺时才有效，而对多数组织，难的是前一半。
detailEn: Kaplan and Norton proposed it in the Harvard Business Review in 1992, starting from an old commonplace: financial numbers are lagging results, gameable by short-term hands, while the processes that create value happen where the reports cannot see. The fix widens the dashboard to four perspectives — financial (the outcome), customer (how you are valued), internal process (which activities must excel), learning and growth (people, information, systems) — not as four equal boxes but as a causal chain read bottom-up: capable staff make capable processes, capable processes win customers, won customers deliver the financials, every link nameable. It quietly corrects a commoner error: profit is the fruit, not the tree, and decomposing a profit target onto everyone's head is asking the fruit to water the tree. Leading and lagging indicators now travel together — lagging ones confirm whether the strategy paid off, leading ones say whether the logic holds. The failure mode is equally classic: it ships as one more appraisal report, ten measures per box, nobody acting on any. The scorecard only works once strategy is clear enough to translate into objectives and gauges, and for most organisations the hard half is upstream.

oneLiner: 流动资产减流动负债——够不够付近期的账，同时别让现金躺着不生息。
oneLinerEn: Current assets minus current liabilities — enough to pay near-term bills without letting cash sit idle.
detail: 利润是账面意见，现金是事实，而两家赚钱的公司可能一家现金紧绷一家现金泛滥——差别就在营运资本。它管的是三类被占用的钱：存货压在仓里、应收挂在客户名下、应付欠着供应商。现金转换周期把占用量化：存货天数加应收天数减应付天数。快时尚把存货天数从九十天压到三十天，释放的不是效率而是可支配现金。零售巨头的经典玩法是把应付天数做长、收现做快，靠负营运资本让供应商变相提供免息融资——但把上游现金流压到极限会把生态压碎，供应商账期拖欠在多数国家有法律与声誉代价。反向的坑是存货“安全垫”：为防断供层层加码，占用的资金最终都计进了成本。所以这条线上真正的本事是区分流动性保险与资金浪费，并且明白一件事：缩短转换周期释放的现金，常常比多赚一单来得更快也更确定。
detailEn: Profit is an opinion, cash is a fact, and two profitable firms can differ utterly — one cash-tight, one flooding — the gap living in working capital. It manages three kinds of money held hostage: inventory sitting in the warehouse, receivables parked at customers, payables owed to suppliers. The cash-conversion cycle quantifies the hostage-taking: days of inventory plus days of receivables minus days of payables. When fast fashion compressed inventory from ninety days to thirty, what was freed was not efficiency but spendable cash. The classic retail play lengthens payables while collecting instantly, running on negative working capital so suppliers effectively lend at zero interest — yet squeeze upstream to the limit and the ecosystem cracks, since late payment carries legal and reputational cost in most jurisdictions. The mirror trap is the inventory cushion: stacking safety stock against every conceivable shortage, then finding the tied-up capital has been quietly booked as cost. The skill on this line is telling liquidity insurance from wasted money, and holding one fact clearly: cash released by shortening the cycle usually arrives faster and surer than cash from one more sale.

oneLiner: 把 ROE 拆成净利率×资产周转×权益乘数，看清回报到底靠赚钱、快转还是加杠杆。
oneLinerEn: Decompose ROE into margin × asset turnover × leverage — see whether returns come from profit, speed or borrowed money.
detail: 杜邦体系（源于通用汽车财务部门）把笼统的股东回报一层层拆开：ROE（权益净利率）= 净利率 × 总资产周转率 × 权益乘数——分别回答“卖得贵不贵”“资产转得快不快”“用了多少别人的钱”。它把“ROE 20%”这个单一数字变成可诊断的三条路径：同样的高回报，可能来自品牌溢价（高净利）、来自薄利多销与高效运营（高周转），也可能来自把杠杆拉满（高乘数）。正因如此它也暴露风险：靠杠杆堆出来的高 ROE 遇到逆风最脆弱，而零售与制造往往靠周转取胜。它是连接利润表与资产负债表的桥，也是把战略归因到运营细节的利器。使用时须当心它仍建在会计口径之上，利润率、周转与杠杆三者如何权衡，最终取决于企业真正的战略取向。
detailEn: The DuPont system (born in General Motors' finance department) peels one aggregate shareholder-return figure layer by layer: ROE = net profit margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier, answering respectively "do you sell dear," "do your assets spin fast," and "how much other people's money did you use." It turns a bare "ROE of 20%" into three diagnosable paths—the same high return may come from brand premium (margin), from thin margins and rapid efficient turnover, or from cranking up leverage (multiplier). That is also why it exposes risk: an ROE propped on leverage is the most fragile against a headwind, while retail and manufacturing often win on turnover. It is the bridge linking the income statement to the balance sheet, and a tool for attributing strategy down to operating detail.

oneLiner: 利润扣掉“占用的资本也要有回报”之后，剩下才是真正创造的价值。
oneLinerEn: Profit less a charge for the capital employed — what remains is value actually created.
detail: 乔尔·斯特恩与 G. 本纳·斯图尔特推广的经济增加值 = 税后经营利润 − （资本成本率 × 占用资本）。它的锋利之处在于提醒：会计利润为正不等于创造价值——若回报低于资本的机会成本，账面在赚、经济在亏，股东其实被侵蚀了。它迫使管理者为占用的每一元资本负责，抑制盲目扩张与“为增长而增长”，常被用来设计更贴近价值的高管激励与内部考核。思科在 1990 年代把它当作全公司运营罗盘而名声大噪。批评者则指出它仍依赖会计假设、容易被资本成本率的拍定人为操纵，且对初创与长周期行业不够友好——本质上它是对“自由现金流”的一个会计近似。
detailEn: Popularized by Joel Stern and G. Bennett Stewart, economic value added equals after-tax operating profit minus (the cost of capital × capital employed). Its sharpness is the reminder that positive accounting profit is not the same as value creation—if the return falls short of capital's opportunity cost, the books show a gain while the economics show a loss and shareholders are quietly eroded. It forces managers to answer for every dollar of capital tied up, curbing blind expansion and "growth for growth's sake," and is often used to design executive pay and internal scorecards closer to value; Cisco made it famous as a company-wide operating compass in the 1990s. Critics note it still leans on accounting assumptions, can be gamed by the eyeballed cost-of-capital rate, and sits awkwardly with startups and long-cycle industries—at bottom it is an accounting proxy for free cash flow.

oneLiner: 用少数几个能真正反映成效的量化指标，把“干得好不好”变成看得见、可追踪。
oneLinerEn: A few quantified indicators that truly reflect performance, turning 'are we doing well' into something visible and trackable.
detail: KPI 把战略与目标翻译成可衡量的关键数字，用于监控进展、发现问题、驱动改进。好的 KPI 遵循 SMART、紧扣“关键”而非堆指标——什么都能量往往意味着什么都不重要；它还要警惕古德哈特定律“一旦指标成为目标，它就不再是好指标”，否则团队会刷数字而偏离真实价值。它与 OKR 互补：OKR 定方向与野心、激发对齐，KPI 盯常态运营与达标；也呼应平衡计分卡——后者提醒别只看财务一维。
detailEn: A KPI translates strategy and goals into measurable key numbers used to monitor progress, surface problems and drive improvement. Good KPIs are SMART and stay 'key' rather than a pile of metrics — if you measure everything, it often means nothing matters; they must also guard against Goodhart's law, 'when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure', lest teams game the number and drift from real value. KPIs complement OKRs — OKRs set direction and ambition and spark alignment, KPIs watch steady-state performance and attainment — and echo the balanced scorecard, which warns against tracking the financial dimension alone.

oneLiner: 把未来的钱按贴现折算成今天值多少：NPV 为正才创造价值，IRR 是让它归零的回报率。
oneLinerEn: Discount future money to today's value — a positive NPV creates value, and the IRR is the rate that drives it to zero.
detail: 因为“今天的一元比明年的一元值钱”(时间价值)，评估投资要把未来各期现金流按要求的回报率(资本成本)贴现回今天求和，再减去初始投入得到 NPV；NPV 大于零表示收益超过资金成本、值得做，反之毁价值。IRR 则是令 NPV 归零的那个内在回报率，越高越好、须高于资本成本。它比“多久回本”更讲道理，因为它顾到全部现金流与货币时间价值；但两者都依赖贴现率估计，对非常规现金流(正负交替)IRR 可能多个或失真，此时以 NPV 为准。
detailEn: Because a dollar today beats a dollar next year (time value), appraising an investment discounts each future cash flow back to now at the required return (cost of capital), sums them and subtracts the outlay to get NPV; NPV over zero means returns beat the cost of money and it is worth doing, below zero it destroys value. The IRR is the rate that sets NPV to zero — the higher the better, and it must exceed the cost of capital. It beats 'payback period' by honouring all cash flows and the time value of money, but both lean on the discount-rate estimate, and for unconventional cash flows that flip sign the IRR can be multiple or misleading — there, trust NPV.

oneLiner: 选了 A，成本就是被放弃的最好那个 B——真代价常在“你没做的另一件事”里。
oneLinerEn: Choose A and the cost is the best B you forwent — the real price usually sits in the thing you did not do.
detail: 机会成本指为得到某选择而放弃的最佳替代方案的价值，它不进账本却决定取舍：自建团队的钱若投进主业更赚，那“更赚”才是自建的隐藏成本；老板亲自盯生产线的“工资”按他别处能创造的价值算，常高于雇人。它也提醒：已花的钱是沉没成本、不该左右未来，而“用满资源”不等于“用对资源”。在决策树、投资评估与资源配置里，把隐形的“次优选项”显式算进去，才不至于用“看起来没花钱”骗自己。
detailEn: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative you give up to choose something; it never books as an expense yet it decides trade-offs — if cash spent building an in-house team would earn more in the core business, that 'more' is the hidden cost of building; the owner's time supervising a line is priced by the value they would create elsewhere, often above hiring someone. It also warns that money already spent is a sunk cost that should not sway the future, and that using every resource is not using resources well. In decision trees, investment appraisal and allocation, making the invisible runner-up explicit keeps you from fooling yourself that a choice costs nothing.

oneLiner: 机器会旧、软件会过时:把一笔大额资产,按使用年限逐年摊进成本。
oneLinerEn: Machines wear and software ages — spread a big asset's cost over its useful years rather than all at once.
detail: 折旧是把固定资产(厂房、设备、车辆)的购置成本,按其预计使用年限与残值,用系统方法(直线法、加速折旧法等)分摊到各期费用,体现“资产在使用中损耗、其价值随服务流出”。它影响账面利润(折旧是费用但不付现)、税基,也提醒管理者:设备的“成本”不只在买入那天。与之并列的有无形资产的“摊销”。理解折旧才能读懂利润表与现金流为何不同。
detailEn: Depreciation spreads the purchase cost of a fixed asset (a plant, machine, vehicle) over its expected useful life and residual value by a systematic method — straight-line, accelerated and so on — to reflect that the asset wears out and its value flows out as service. It shapes reported profit (a non-cash expense), the tax base, and the manager's view that an asset's cost is not only the day it is bought. The kin concept for intangibles is amortisation. Only by grasping depreciation do you see why the income statement and cash flow differ.

oneLiner: 每期预算从“零”谈起:不默认去年给了多少,每笔钱都要重新证明必要性。
oneLinerEn: Start each budget at zero — no carry-over of last year's amount; every dollar must re-justify itself.
detail: 传统预算常在上期基础上加减,易把历史浪费与低效固化(“去年有,所以今年也该有”)。彼得·派尔提出的零基预算要求:每期假设一切归零,各方案从零论证所需资源与优先次序,按成本效益重新分配。它擅长挤掉沉疴、把资源转向更值的事,却耗时耗力、对稳定运营略显“重”,故现实中多用于费用整顿或阶段性“预算归零”审视,而非年年全套执行。
detailEn: Conventional budgeting adds and subtracts on last year's base, which ossifies past waste (we had it before, so we should again). Pyhrr's zero-based budgeting instead resets to zero each period and requires every program to argue afresh the resources it needs and its priority, allocating by cost-benefit. It is strong at wringing out legacy bloat and shifting resources to what matters more, yet costly and heavy for steady operations — so in practice it is used for expense clean-ups or periodic reset scrutiny rather than full re-runs every year.

oneLiner: 分清“不开张也要付”(固定)与“随量才变”(变动)——它是盈亏平衡与定价的地基。
oneLinerEn: Tell apart what you pay even at zero sales (fixed) from what moves with volume (variable) — the base of breakeven and pricing.
detail: 把成本按性态分成两类:固定成本(租金、月薪、设备折旧)在一定产能内不随产量变;变动成本(原料、计件、运费)随产量正比增减。这个切分带来几个关键判断:经营杠杆(固定占比越高,销量波动被放大到利润上越猛)、单位经济(每多卖一件贡献多少“边际”),以及盈亏平衡点=固定成本÷单件边际贡献。定价、扩产、外包等决策都先问“钱花在固定还是变动上”——固定投入大则风险高但规模回报大。
detailEn: Splitting costs by behaviour: fixed costs (rent, salaries, equipment depreciation) stay put within a capacity range; variable costs (materials, piece-pay, freight) rise in proportion to volume. The cut yields key judgements — operating leverage (the higher the fixed share, the more a sales swing is amplified into profit), unit economics (the contribution each extra sale adds) and the breakeven point, fixed cost divided by contribution per unit. Pricing, scaling and outsourcing all start from whether this money is fixed or variable — heavy fixed spend means higher risk but greater reward at scale.

term: CAPM 资本资产定价模型
oneLiner: 收益要补偿风险，但市场只补偿“分散不掉”的系统性风险——系数越大，要求的回报越高。
oneLinerEn: Return must pay for risk, but the market only rewards the systematic risk you cannot diversify away—the higher the coefficient, the higher the required return.
detail: 模型给出一条简洁公式：某资产的预期收益等于无风险利率加上该资产相对大盘的敏感度（贝塔）乘以市场风险溢价。它把风险分成可被分散消除的非系统性风险与逃不掉的系统性风险，认为理性市场只为后者付费。它被广泛用于估算股权成本、给项目设定“至少该赚多少才算够”的门槛。正因假设苛刻（人人理性、持有同一市场组合）而常被质疑，但作为思维的基准线，它把“高收益究竟来自承担哪种风险”说得极其透彻。
detailEn: The model yields one compact formula: an asset's expected return equals the risk-free rate plus its sensitivity to the whole market (beta) times the market risk premium. It splits risk into non-systematic risk that diversification can erase and systematic risk you cannot escape, holding that a rational market pays only for the latter. It is widely used to estimate the cost of equity and to set the hurdle of what a project must at least earn. Harsh assumptions (universal rationality, one shared market portfolio) draw steady criticism, yet as a baseline it makes strikingly clear which kind of risk a high return really comes from.

term: WACC 加权平均资本成本
oneLiner: 企业用的钱既有债也有股，按各自占比加权平均出一个综合成本——它就是估值的折现尺。
oneLinerEn: A firm runs on debt and equity alike; weighting each by its share gives one blended cost—the discount yardstick of valuation.
detail: 股权成本常用资本资产定价模型估算，债务成本看利率、并因利息可在税前列支而打个折（所谓税盾），再按负债与权益的比例加权，得到综合资本成本。它是净现值与现金流折现估值里那个折现率：数值越低，同样现金流算出的价值越高，所以优化资本结构、降低融资成本会直接抬升企业价值。风险越高的公司这项成本越高、越难为长远项目融资——它把“资本并非免费”量化到了每一个决策上。
detailEn: The cost of equity is often estimated with the capital asset pricing model; the cost of debt reads off interest rates and, because interest is tax-deductible, is discounted by a so-called tax shield; weighting the two by their shares gives the blended figure. It is the discount rate inside net present value and discounted-cash-flow valuation: the lower it runs, the higher the value of the same cash flows, so tuning capital structure and cutting funding cost lift firm value directly. Riskier firms face a higher cost and struggle to fund long projects—it quantifies capital is never free in every decision.

oneLiner: 别把间接费用一律摊到产量上：先算每项作业花多少钱，再按谁触发了它来分摊，成本才不冤枉。
oneLinerEn: Do not spread overhead on volume alone: cost each activity first, then charge it to those who trigger it, so no product is wrongly over- or under-charged.
detail: 传统成本法用单一基准（如工时、产量）分摊制造费用，常让大批量简单产品暗中补贴了小批量复杂产品。作业成本法改为按作业归集成本——备料、质检、调试、订单处理各算一笔，再用成本动因（批次、次数、工时）追溯到具体产品与客户，从而揭示复杂小单的隐形代价，帮助定价、外包与流程改进。代价是核算更繁琐、需要较细的数据，故多用在间接费用占比高、产品多样化的企业。
detailEn: Traditional costing spreads overhead on one base such as labour hours or output volume, often letting high-volume simple products quietly subsidise low-volume complex ones. Activity-based costing instead pools cost by activity—setup, inspection, changeover, order handling each gets its own figure—then traces it to specific products and customers via cost drivers (batches, counts, hours), exposing the hidden cost of fussy small orders to guide pricing, outsourcing and process repair. The price is heavier bookkeeping and finer data, so it suits firms where overhead is a large share and the product mix is diverse.

oneLiner: 企业靠债还是靠股来撑？两者比例既影响成本与风险，也放大收益——这是杠杆的双刃。
oneLinerEn: Prop the firm up with debt or equity? The ratio shapes cost and risk and magnifies return alike—the double edge of leverage.
detail: 债务便宜（利息可抵税、要求回报低于股权）却要按期偿付、放大下行风险，甚至推向破产；权益没有还本压力，但成本更高且不抵税。莫迪利安尼与米勒在理想世界里证明资本结构不影响价值，而现实中的税盾、财务困境成本与管理层动机打破了这份中性，形成权衡理论：适度负债提升价值，越过临界点后风险成本反噬。杠杆既能放大股东回报，也能放大亏损——稳健的公司往往留足举债的余力，以备不时之需。
detailEn: Debt is cheap (interest is tax-deductible and its required return sits below equity's) but must be repaid on schedule, amplifies downside risk and can push toward failure; equity carries no repayment pressure yet costs more and gets no tax break. Modigliani and Miller proved capital structure irrelevant to value in an ideal world, while real tax shields, financial-distress cost and managerial motive break that neutrality into a trade-off theory: moderate debt lifts value until, past a tipping point, risk cost bites back. Leverage magnifies shareholder return and loss alike—sound firms keep spare borrowing capacity for a rainy day.
